I implemented `tax_for` in `src/billing/tax.py`, but it rounds half-even (banker's rounding), not half-up. A project decision in EngramDB says tax uses `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`, agreed with finance in March 2026, and says not to use `ROUND_HALF_UP`. I haven't run the function or any tests.

It takes `amount_cents` and a decimal-fraction `rate` (0.0825 for 8.25%). It returns integer cents with no float arithmetic.

A second decision says Quebec (`region == "CA-QC"`) customers are taxed per line, rounding each line's tax and then summing. Other customers are taxed once on the subtotal. `tax_for` doesn't take a region, so that branching belongs in the caller. The caller should call `tax_for` per line for QC and once on `line_total` otherwise.

If finance has since changed the rule to half-up, tell me and I'll switch it and update the memory.

An edit hook flagged the "Invoice PDF rendering" memory (`01a106b0-e819`) as possibly affected by this change. I haven't checked it, and a tax function that isn't called yet shouldn't affect PDF rendering.
